description: We are Young Tech, a team of passionate young innovators from South Sudan interested in robotics, AI, programming, engineering, and space science. We love learning, sharing ideas, and creating solutions to real-world problems. We welcome creative and curious people with skills in coding, research, design, engineering, or simply a passion for technology. Experience is welcome, but curiosity, commitment, and teamwork matter most.
summary: AgriSouth AI is a prototype decision-support platform created to help farmers in South Sudan make better-informed planting choices. It combines crop selection, crop rotation, intercropping, and planting-season tools in one dashboard. Farmers can choose a region and enter details such as soil type, pH, and previous harvests. The platform then shows crop options and rotation plans alongside NASA-based views of soil moisture, rainfall, and climate, helping users compare choices based on environmental conditions and crop needs. It also includes farm-zone and harvest-history tools, reporting features, and an AI Agronomist that can answer field-related questions.
details:
AgriSouth AI is a web-based agricultural decision-support prototype designed to help farmers in South Sudan make more informed planting decisions. It combines crop selection, crop rotation, intercropping, and planting-season guidance in a single dashboard. The platform is intended to help farmers explore their options using farm data, environmental observations, crop characteristics, and agricultural knowledge.

Farmers can choose a region and enter or review information such as soil type, pH, soil moisture, and previous harvests. The Crop Selection tool uses these details to show suitable crop options and their key characteristics. The Rotation Plan tool builds on previous harvests to suggest possible crop sequences across seasons. The Intercropping tool helps users compare crop combinations and their potential land-use benefits. These features are meant to support comparison and exploration, not to predict guaranteed yields or outcomes.

The platform also includes several supporting tools. The Planting Season Guide provides seasonal guidance based on location and climate information. NASA Soil Moisture shows soil-moisture observations and related satellite data. Rainfall & Climate Data presents rainfall and climate views for the selected region. Farm Soil & Zone Map helps users view farm plots and soil zones. Previous Harvests & Trends allows farmers to track crop history over time. Export Season Reports generates summaries of crop and seasonal information. AI Agronomist Chat offers a question-and-answer feature for field-related topics, and Crop & Soil Vision AI provides image-based support within the application.

The dashboard brings together NASA-related soil-moisture, rainfall, and climate views with farmer-provided crop and soil information. These data sources provide useful environmental context across wider areas, but they should not be treated as direct measurements of a specific farm plot. The application considers location, soil conditions, pH, previous crops, seasonal conditions, crop requirements, and farmer priorities such as food production, water conservation, and soil health. At the same time, farmer experience, local agricultural advice, and reliable local research remain important when interpreting the results.

The project was built using Python for data processing and agricultural calculations, HTML for structure, CSS for styling, JavaScript for interactive maps, charts, and user interactions, and SQL for storing and managing farmer and agricultural data. Its main idea is to bring these tools together in one place, present several options clearly, and help farmers compare them more easily.
